home_intro: Pianist Misha Galant is the 2025 winner of the National Federation of Music Clubs Young Artist Competition and a 2020 Gilmore Young Artist. He has performed with the Fort Worth Symphony, Rochester Philharmonic, and Utah Symphony, and makes his home in Salt Lake City, where the Wasatch mountains are never far from the practice room.
biography: Born into a family of musicians, Misha Galant began piano lessons at the age of six with his mother, Olya Katsman. During high school, he received guidance from Sharon Mann and Yoshikazu Nagai of the San Francisco Conservatory of Music. Other formative teachers include Tatiana Zelikman of the Gnesin Russian Academy of Music in Moscow and Dr. Yu-Jane Yang of Weber State University in Utah. He went on to graduate from Columbia University, where he studied piano with Joseph Kalichstein through the Columbia-Juilliard Exchange, while also earning degrees in Data Science and Russian Literature. In 2023, he earned a Master’s degree in Piano Performance under Dr. Viktor Valkov at the University of Utah. He later completed a second Master’s in Atmospheric Sciences in 2025, also at the University of Utah, under the guidance of Dr. John Horel. His thesis focused on evaporation dynamics in the regions surrounding the Great Salt Lake.

Misha gave his first full solo recital at age 12 and made his orchestral debut at 13, performing Chopin’s Piano Concerto No. 1 with the Oakland East Bay Symphony. He has since performed with the Fort Worth Symphony, Rochester Philharmonic, Utah Symphony, and the California Youth Symphony, touring with the latter in Austria and Italy in performances of Gershwin’s Rhapsody in Blue. He is a prizewinner of the inaugural Van Cliburn Junior Competition and the Eastman Piano Competition (2015), as well as a semifinalist in the Gina Bachauer and New Orleans International Piano Competitions (2024). From 2015 to 2020, he performed extensively across California as a member of the MTAC’s prestigious Young Artist Guild and was named one of two Gilmore Young Artists in the U.S. in 2020. Most recently, he was named the 2025 winner of the National Federation of Music Clubs (NFMC) Young Artist Competition, receiving a $20,000 award and a two-year performance contract at venues across the United States.

Additionally, Misha is an avid chamber musician and enjoys performing benefit concerts for retirement communities and charitable causes. In 2021, he raised over $1,000 through performances for Haiti earthquake relief, and in 2022, he raised more than $8,500 for Ukraine war relief. Outside of his musical and academic pursuits, Misha enjoys hiking, trail running, and skiing, and was a member of Columbia University’s Division I swim team, training twenty hours per week.
Misha currently resides in Salt Lake City and works full time as a data analyst and environmental consultant for Trinity Consultants, an environmental consulting firm.

mountains_intro: To balance the long hours at the piano, I spend as much of my free time outdoors as I can. Living in Utah means the best of both worlds: a concert hall in the valley and granite ridges an hour's drive away. Here are a few of my favorite adventures.
